// Part: room: bedroom 6 (interior designer's part). Bedroom over the kitchen: the bed on the north wall as the focal
// piece, a barrel and a chest as storage, a nightstand each side, a reading table by the east window, a red rug, and one
// hanging lantern on an iron chain as the room's light, with candles on the tables. Only the inner air box
// [51,11,64]..[57,16,68] is written; the door is on the west wall at x50 z66 and the windows are on the east wall x58.
import { layers, B, bed } from "/Volumes/ext1/swe/repos/minecraft-design/tools/src/build.mjs";

export function build(g) {
  // Floor row y11, origin (51, 11, 64): rows run along +x (x51..57), successive rows along +z (z64..68).
  // The bed is placed by bed() below, so its cells stay blank here.
  const legend = {
    b: "barrel",
    f: "dark_oak_fence",
    k: ["chest", { facing: "south", type: "single" }],
    R: "red_carpet",
    c:["candle", { candles: "1", lit: "true" }],
    p: "flower_pot",
    L: ["lantern", { hanging: "false", waterlogged: "false" }],
    s: ["dark_oak_slab", { type: "top" }],
  };
  const rows11 = [
    "b f f k", // z64: barrel (51), nightstand (53) by the bed head, nightstand (55), chest dresser (57)
    "       ", // z65: bed foot at x54 (bed() below)
    "      f", // z66: table post (57) under the east window; the chair (56) is set below
    "  RR   ", // z67: red rug under the room's centre
    "  RR   ", // z68
  ];
  const rows12 = [
    "p L p c", // flower pot on the barrel, standing lantern on the nightstand, flower pot on the other nightstand, candle on the chest
    "       ",
    "      s", // table top slab (top half, sits on the fence post at 57,11,66)
    "       ",
    "       ",
  ];
  const rows13 = [
    "       ",
    "       ",
    "      c", // lit candle on the table
    "       ",
    "       ",
  ];
  layers(g, [51, 11, 64], legend, [rows11, rows12, rows13]);

  bed(g, [54, 11, 65], "north", "red"); // head at (54,11,64) against the north wall, foot toward the room
  g.set(56, 11, 66, ...B.stairs("dark_oak", "west", "bottom")); // chair: back on the west, seat toward the table
  g.set(51, 11, 67, ...B.lantern(false)); // standing lantern by the door, lights the far corner
  g.set(54, 16, 67, ...B.chain("y")); // hanging lantern on a chain under the ceiling, over the rug
  g.set(54, 15, 67, ...B.lantern(true));
}

input.summary:
parts/room-26.mjs (bedroom 6) is still unbuilt: its 21 writes are all refused because the shell owns every cell of the room's air box (210/210, placed as air). Off-palette is clear: all 11 block ids the room uses are in palette.json and mcd blocks --check reports none unknown.
I did not edit the file. Every cell it could write to is shell-owned, so no move inside the room box can clear the refusal.
make.sh still writes build.nbt (the roof and the other parts are unaffected), but this room contributes no blocks.
left: REFUSED 21 (unfixable inside parts/room-26.mjs): runParts' owned set (minecraft-design/tools/src/build.mjs ~l.191-243) adds every write an earlier part makes, air included, and parts/shell.mjs fills the whole wing interior with air (box(37,61,58,75) carves x38..57 z62..74 y4..16). The 210 cells of the room box [51,11,64]..[57,16,68] are all shell-owned air, so the room's bed, barrel, chests, lanterns and rug are refused wherever they go. The fix belongs upstream, not in this part: either runParts counts only non-air writes as owned (with doorways kept through reserved cells), or the shell stops pre-filling room interiors with air. Not done here because the task said to fix only room-26.mjs and never edit another module.

Off-palette: none for room-26 (all its ids are in palette.json and mcd blocks --check reports none unknown), but its refused writes never reached the off-palette check, so re-run after the lock is fixed.

Outside this part, still open for the roof: roof stage reports off-palette tuff_brick_slab, tuff_bricks, cobbled_deepslate_stairs/slab, tuff_brick_stairs, polished_deepslate_slab/stairs, stone_brick_slab (fix roof.json).

waste.what: Working out which shell cells own the room's box: I ran a MCD_PARTS_CELLS dump and a 210-cell loop by hand to learn that the whole box is shell-owned air.
waste.cost: about 4 tool calls and one extra build run
waste.tool: runParts refusal report should name the owning part and whether the owned cell is air or solid (it lists 8 of 21 and truncates via slice(0,8)); add a `mcd owned <build> --part name --box x0,y0,z0,x1,y1,z1` that prints free vs owned cells per box.

waste.what: Checking off-palette ids by hand: refused writes never reach the off-palette check, so I had to list the room's ids and check them against palette.json myself.
waste.cost: one mcd blocks --check call plus reading palette.json
waste.tool: runParts should run the palette check on the intended writes, not only on accepted ones, so a refused part still reports off-palette blocks.
